title: SpeedShield: emergency throughput & first-token lag across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Nora Patel
description: Multiple premium customers reported sudden TTFT regressions and throughput drops (tokens/sec) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments after the 1.22 kernel-selector rollout and the new prefetch reservation heuristic. Impact: increased first-token latency, lower tokens/sec for multi-turn chat workloads, and cascading autoscaler churn in Dedicated pools. This ticket coordinates an urgent mitigation, root-cause verification, and follow-up engineering work to prevent recurrence.
comments: 2025-02-11 06:45 UTC - Nora Patel: Pager triggered from customer A (Enterprise, Dedicated) for 3x TTFT regression over last 30m. Alerts: first_byte_p50 up, token_throughput down. Created incident channel and engaged SRE + runtime oncall.

2025-02-11 07:02 UTC - Diego Martinez: Observed same signature in Hosted region eu-west-1 and in two Private customer clusters. Initial hypothesis: new kernel-selector change (runtime-1.22) misclassifies mixed-context requests and forces quantized int8 variants with a prefetch reservation that thrashes KV cache. Opening triage runbook.

2025-02-11 07:25 UTC - Aisha Kaur (SRE): Deployed temporary rate-limiter adjustment for impacted routes and set dedicated autoscaler to fixed capacity to avoid thrash. Noted that token eviction counts spike shortly after model fan-out events.

2025-02-11 08:10 UTC - Diego Martinez: Rolled back kernel-selector flag to previous stable heuristics for a subset of canary hosts (10% of traffic) — immediate reduction in TF-T and tokens/sec recovered by ~40% for canary. Pushed rollback to 50% while we confirm.

2025-02-11 09:00 UTC - PM triage (Liam O'Connor): Informed customers via private escalation channel with ETA for full mitigation. Escalation includes customers B, C, and D. Created customer-facing status note in Confluence.

2025-02-11 11:35 UTC - Diego Martinez: Identified a bug in prefetch reservation where multi-model fanout requests reserved prefetched KV slots but did not account for interleaved contexts, causing premature eviction of active contexts under burst. Patch prepared to enforce 'prefetch-reserve-per-model' and to add a soft quota for KV prefetch per session.
2025-02-11 14:50 UTC - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789 - 'prefetch: reserve-per-model guard and eviction safety' (linked). Canary deploy scheduled at 15:30 UTC.

2025-02-11 15:50 UTC - SRE (Aisha): Canary metrics after PR apply: first_token_p50 improved 55% on canary hosts; tokens/sec moved toward baseline; no new OOMs observed. Rolling to 80% with monitoring.

2025-02-11 18:10 UTC - Diego Martinez: Full rollout of PR to all hosted clusters and an auto-upgrade package for Dedicated customers with opt-in patch (support will coordinate). For Private customers we provided the patch bundle and a manual upgrade guide.

2025-02-11 19:45 UTC - Nora Patel: Customer follow-ups: B and C reported restoration to pre-incident performance; D needs manual assistance for on-prem upgrade due to air-gapped constraints. Support ticket created: SUP-88412.

2025-02-12 09:00 UTC - Diego Martinez: Post-mortem note draft started. Early root cause: interaction between kernel-selector heuristic (favored quantized variant during fanout) + prefetch-reservation logic that double-counted interleaved contexts under multiplexed sessions. Contributing factor: insufficient perf testing for high-fanout mixed-context workloads in pre-release matrix.

2025-02-12 10:30 UTC - Action items assigned: 1) Add automated mixed-context fanout perf tests to CI (owner: Priya Singh, estimate 3). 2) Add telemetry for per-session prefetch reservations and eviction waterfall (owner: Marco Chen, estimate 2). 3) Introduce safe-fallback policy in router to avoid model-fanout for tail-latency-sensitive routes (owner: Diego, estimate 5).

2025-02-12 11:00 UTC - Diego Martinez: Marking mitigation as deployed and stable for hosted + dedicated. Private customers: three clusters still pending upgrade; support coordinating with on-prem teams. Will transition to 'In Progress' remediation and PM review.
2025-02-12 11:15 UTC - Nora Patel: Notifying Customer Success and SOC of post-deploy metrics. Scheduling 2025-02-20 meeting to review long-term fixes and SLAs for kernel-selector changes.
2025-02-12 12:00 UTC - QA (Elena Ruiz): Confirmed regression test case reproduces TTFT delta locally when prefetch-reserve miscounts interleaved contexts. Adding to nightly regression.
2025-02-12 12:45 UTC - Diego Martinez: Linking incident to runtime-1.22 release notes and gating future kernel-selector changes behind canary thresholds + perf gate in CI.

2025-02-12 13:00 UTC - Diego Martinez: Pending tasks - finalize postmortem, follow up on private customer upgrades, implement router safe-fallback, add telemetry dashboards. Targeting Done for mitigation by 2025-02-15 and remediation actions in next two cycles.
